findings.title: Footle's window keydown has no dialog/input guard: Enter on a sheet button submits a guess and cancels the button
findings.claim: FootballWordle attaches a window-level keydown listener (:291-297) that only checks modifier keys — unlike ReviewScreen.jsx:256-257, it never checks e.target (INPUT/TEXTAREA) or whether a [role=dialog] is open. While a puzzle is 'playing', the How-to-play sheet opened by the ? button (:409 → App.jsx:8040 setHowToPlay('wordle') → sheet at App.jsx:8407) is a sibling overlay, and useModalA11y focuses its first button 'Got it ✓'. Pressing Enter to activate that button is intercepted: preventDefault() cancels the button's Enter activation so the sheet does not close, and handleKey('ENTER') runs submitGuess behind the sheet — with a complete word on the board this commits a guess, which the state effect (:183-186) writes to localStorage and syncs to profiles.wordle_state; with an incomplete word it shakes the row. Backspace on the sheet likewise deletes a board letter (:294). The same unguarded pattern is in HotStreakEngine/TrueFalseEngine's Enter/Space → advance() listeners (App.jsx:2366, :2495), though their window is the 400-2400ms hold.
findings.evidence: FootballWordle.jsx:291-298: onKeyDown checks only metaKey/ctrlKey/altKey, then Enter → preventDefault + ENTER; Backspace → preventDefault + DEL; letters → typed. `grep -n 'tagName\|isContentEditable\|closest(' src/games/FootballWordle.jsx` returns nothing. handleKey (:269-276) only bails when state.status !== 'playing'. useModalA11y.js:112-117 focuses the first focusable in the sheet, i.e. 'Got it ✓' (App.jsx:8418). ReviewScreen.jsx:256-257 shows the guard the app already uses elsewhere.
findings.howToVerify: Desktop browser: open /play → Footle on an unplayed day, type a full-length word with the physical keyboard (do not press Enter), click the ? button to open How to play, then press Enter. Expected defect: the sheet stays open (the focused 'Got it ✓' does not fire), the board behind it flips a submitted guess, and localStorage key wordle_state:<today> now contains that guess. Control: press Backspace in the same sheet → a letter disappears from the board under the sheet.

findings.title: Rate prompt: Escape/back-gesture dismissal is not logged as 'rate-prompt-dismissed' while backdrop and 'Maybe later' are
findings.snippet: useModalA11y({ isOpen: !!showRatePrompt, onClose: () => setShowRatePrompt(false), ref: ratePromptRef });
findings.claim: The web rate sheet counts its outcomes (rate-prompt-shown / loving / not-really / store-tap / store-unreachable / dismissed{how}) and the ledger lists 'dismissed (view + how)' as an instrumented outcome. But only two of the three dismissal gestures write the row: the backdrop tap (App.jsx:8363) and 'Maybe later' (:8401) call loopEvent('rate-prompt-dismissed', …); the useModalA11y onClose at :8020 — which is what Escape, the iOS swipe-back/browser back button and the Android hardware back (closeTopModal) all route through — just calls setShowRatePrompt(false). On mobile web (most of the base) the back gesture is a common way out of a bottom sheet, so 'shown' minus the logged outcomes leaves an unexplained remainder that reads as 'closed the tab', and every conversion rate computed against 'shown' vs 'dismissed' is off by that remainder. The web budget is three asks per lifetime, so each unlogged dismissal is a third of the data.
findings.evidence: App.jsx:8020 onClose has no loopEvent; :8363 backdrop and :8401 'Maybe later' both log rate-prompt-dismissed with a `how`. useModalA11y.js:80-82 (popstate) and :93-105 (closeTopModal) fire the same onClose for back gestures; :143-147 for Escape.

findings.title: lists-staleness runs in the build WITHOUT --strict, so a stale list never fails it
findings.claim: The build chain in package.json line 12 invokes `node scripts/lists-staleness.mjs` with no flag. The script's own header says `--strict # exit 1 on findings (CI/build)`, but the build never passes it, so every finding is printed as a ⚠️ line in ~40 lines of build output and the process exits 0. A /lists table that has gone two seasons stale (the exact rot this script exists to catch, and the reason it sits in the chain) is reported as a warning and the build, and the Vercel deploy that runs it, go green.
findings.evidence: `BIQ_YEAR=2030 node scripts/lists-staleness.mjs` printed 27 stale-list findings ("23/50 lists look current") and exited 0. `grep -n lists-staleness package.json` shows the build line calls it bare; only the unused `lists:stale` script exists and it is not strict either. Today's real run prints "✅ 50 lists, none stale", so nothing has yet exercised the failure path.

findings.title: api/c.js loop-hit write never reads the response status; 0 rows all time is indistinguishable from 'no traffic'
findings.claim: The share-loop instrument added on 2026-09-04 (f043131) POSTs to PostgREST and discards the Response: `res.ok`/status are never read, the whole block sits inside `try {} catch {}`, and the only trace is a console.log that goes to the Vercel stream nobody reads (per the file's own comment). A 401 from a missing/rotated VITE_SUPABASE_KEY on the edge runtime, a 404 from a renamed RPC, or a 429 from the rate cap all look exactly like a successful write. The comment on line 55 records that this precise failure already happened once ("the first deploy of this wrote nothing"), and the code still cannot tell. Production today: funnel_events has ZERO 'loop-hit' rows all time, three days after shipping — consistent with the low share-daily volume (1 event since 09-04) but equally consistent with a dead write, and nothing in the code can distinguish the two.
findings.evidence: Read-only prod SQL: `select count(*) from funnel_events where event='loop-hit'` = 0, min(created_at) = null; share-daily since 2026-09-04 = 1 row; challenge_events last row 2026-08-30. api/c.js lines 63-73: Promise.race([fetch(...).catch(()=>{}), 800ms timer]) inside try{}catch{} with no status read.

findings.title: Day-2 email decides 'yesterday' and 'today' on the server's UTC date — the defect v1_8 documented and fixed for reminders, re-shipped for email
findings.snippet:
and public.played_on(u.id, (current_date - 1))
    and not public.played_on(u.id, current_date)
findings.claim: Real condition: 'signed up yesterday (their day), played that day, has not come back on their day 2'. Proxy: Postgres `current_date` (UTC) for both days, with `played_on` (line 22: 'has this user played on a given UTC date?') bucketing `scores.created_at` by UTC midnight while the same function's Footle branch reads `wordle_state` keys that the client writes by LOCAL date — so one function mixes two calendars. Concrete input: a New York player signs up 15:00 local on day D (19:00Z), plays at signup, plays again 21:00 local the same evening (02:00Z on D+1). Every hourly run on UTC day D+1 sees played_on(current_date)=true and skips them; on D+2 their created_at is outside the [current_date-1, current_date) window, so they are never selected. The most engaged west-of-UTC signups — exactly who v1_8 said the reminder was silently skipping — never get the day-2 email, while an Oslo player who plays at 00:30 local on D+1 (22:30Z on D) reads as 'played yesterday, not today' and IS mailed although they were in the app half an hour ago.
findings.evidence: v1_12 lines 22-40 define played_on on `p_day::timestamptz` (UTC midnight) OR `wordle_state -> p_day::text` (client-local key). Lines 55-63 select on `current_date - 1` / `current_date`. supabase/migrations/v1_8_reminder_local_window.sql lines 7-20 describe the identical UTC-midnight boundary as defect #1 with the same New York / Oslo examples and fix it by shifting the boundary by the subscriber's offset; v1_12 (a later migration) does not. No tz offset is available for this audience (they are selected precisely for having no push subscription), so the fix cannot be a copy of v1_8's — but the current selector is wrong in both directions.
findings.howToVerify: Read-only on prod (project blcisypmngimqkwxrrdm): select u.id, u.created_at, min(s.created_at) as first_play_utc_today from auth.users u join public.scores s on s.user_id=u.id where u.created_at >= (current_date-1)::timestamptz and u.created_at < current_date::timestamptz and s.created_at >= current_date::timestamptz and s.created_at < current_date::timestamptz + interval '6 hours' group by 1,2; — any row is a signup who played between 00:00Z and 06:00Z (evening in the Americas, still their signup day) and is excluded by select_day2_email_candidates() today and out of its created_at window tomorrow; confirm with select count(*) from public.select_day2_email_candidates() c where c.user_id in (<those ids>) → 0. Code-only check: grep -n 'current_date' supabase/migrations/v1_12_email_campaigns.sql and compare with the boundary comment at lines 7-20 of v1_8_reminder_local_window.sql.

findings.title: Rate prompt counts any Mac desktop click as an Apple store tap — 'Macintosh' stands in for 'has an App Store to review in'
findings.claim: Real condition: 'this browser can open the iOS App Store review sheet'. Proxy: the UA contains Macintosh (added for iPadOS 13+ desktop-mode UAs). The web rate prompt renders on desktop (App.jsx:6846 and :7208 gate on webRatePromptEligible(), not on platform), so Chrome/Safari on a Mac laptop hits this branch, is sent to apps.apple.com/...?action=write-review for an iPhone app, and is logged as `rate-store-tap {store:'apple'}` — the same event as a real iPhone tap. The comment eight lines below says desktop taps must be counted as `rate-store-unreachable` because grouping them 'would inflate the only conversion number this funnel has'; this branch does exactly that for every Mac. The repo's own store detector disagrees with it: StoreBadge.jsx:15 `isIOSUA` requires Mac + maxTouchPoints > 1, so the same visitor gets no badge on the homepage but an 'Apple store tap' in the rating funnel.

findings.title: Live submit_answer lacks the repo's documented -1 (timeout) guard before writing room_answers
